output.text: The sky looks blue because of how air molecules scatter sunlight. Sunlight contains all colors, and short blue wavelengths scatter more strongly than long red ones when they strike particles in the atmosphere. This effect is called Rayleigh scattering. The scattered blue light reaches your eyes from every direction, so the whole sky glows blue. At sunset light travels a longer path, most blue is scattered away, and the sky turns red and orange.
